items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Topics 19:1
items.html: The vessels of the face [Panim] have their source in the Nekudim of the smallness, for the light of the openings of the eyes spread in the vessels of HBD HGT of the seven lower [Sefirot], up to their Chazeh, and only beneath them was spread the Parsa, which is the conclusion of the second restriction. And it is found that in these vessels there is no power of restriction at all, for they were completed above the Parsa. And the vessels of the posterior [Achoraim] have their source in the vessels from the Chazeh and below of the seven lower [Sefirot] of Nekudim, which are found beneath the Parsa of Nekudim. At the time of the greatness of Nekudim they joined with the vessels of the face of the seven lower [Sefirot] and became one Partzuf, and received the upper light together with the vessels of the face. Therefore both of them, the face and the posterior, were broken together. For the vessels of the posterior were not fit to receive the upper light while they were below the Parsa, and therefore they caused a breaking also to the vessels of the face, which were then joined with them. Therefore, at the time of the correction, the vessels of the posterior ascend above the Parsa, and there it is possible for them to receive the upper light. Nevertheless, there remains a great difference between the vessels of the face — which from their source are in the aspect of Atzilut, that is, above the Parsa, and whose entire breaking was only by the power of their joining with the Achoraim — and the vessels of the posterior, which from their source are of the aspect below the Parsa, and whose breaking was because of themselves. Therefore the power of judgment rides upon them, and for this reason they are called Achoraim [posteriors]. And likewise the vessels of the externality of the Partzuf are so called, because from their source they are outside Atzilut — that is, outside the Parsa. (Item 1).
